When required, you will escalate unresolved issues to higher support levels, ensuring continuity of service and a high standard of user experience in a fast-paced, technology-driven environment. Key Responsibilities: Answer incoming service desk calls and log incidents and requests accurately in the call tracking system. Hands-on experience with incident management and ticketing tools. Basic troubleshooting knowledge of Windows operating systems and standard enterprise applications. Familiarity with knowledge management tools and ITIL-based support processes. Strong customer service skills with the ability to handle users professionally in high-volume environments. Fluency in Italian both written and spoken.

review_candidates.title: Executive Coordinator | Egypt
review_candidates.description: Job Requisition ID: 181108 Established in the 1930s as a trading business, Al-Futtaim Group today is one of the most diversified and progressive, privately held regional businesses headquartered in Dubai, United A”rab Emirates. Structured into five operating divisions; automotive, financial services, real estate, retail and healthcare; employing more than 35,000 employees across more than 20 countries in the Middle East, Asia and Africa, Al-Futtaim Group partners with over 200 of the world's most admired and innovative brands. Al-Futtaim Group’s entrepreneurship and relentless customer focus enables the organisation to continue to grow and expand; responding to the changing needs of our customers within the societies in which we operate. By upholding our values of respect, excellence, collaboration and integrity; Al-Futtaim Group continues to enrich the lives and aspirations of our customers each and every day. Role Purpose The role provides high-trust, high-impact coordination support. The role is designed for a confident, socially intelligent individual who can listen carefully, read situations, act decisively, and solve problems in real time. The role is not about language but about social behavior. This is not a traditional finance or administrative role role. Success depends on judgement, behavior, responsiveness, and execution; the ability to engage with people at all levels, manage time flawlessly, and translate conversations into action. Key Accountabilities Executive & Stakeholder Interaction Engage confidently with senior leaders, stakeholders, and teams at all levels. Listen actively, understand context quickly, and respond appropriately in the moment. Represent the office with professionalism, confidence, and strong social awareness. Real-Time Action & Problem Solving Translate discussions into clear actions, priorities, and next steps—often on the spot. Anticipate issues before they escalate and propose practical solutions. Resolve day-to-day challenges independently, knowing when to escalate. Coordination & Follow-Through Manage complex schedules, meetings, and priorities with excellent time discipline. Track commitments, decisions, and actions to ensure nothing is missed. Ensure accuracy in details, documentation, and communication at all times. Execution Excellence Maintain strong structure and organisation across multiple workstreams. Balance speed with accuracy in a fast-moving environment. Continuously improve ways of working through better organisation and judgement. Requirements: Core Attributes (Non-Negotiable) Exceptional communicator and listener – understands what is said and what is implied. Strong social behaviour and judgement – reads people and situations well. Confident with healthy self-esteem – comfortable engaging with senior leaders. Decisive and action-oriented – able to act immediately when needed. Highly organised with strong time management. Detail-accurate – nothing slips through the cracks. Experience Minimum 3 years’ experience in roles involving coordination, execution, or ownership of outcomes (e.g. project coordination/management, operations, business development, sales execution, or leadership support). Direct responsibility for follow-ups, tracking, or delivery, not just participation (e.g. owning action logs, deadlines, stakeholders, or outcomes). Advanced Excel and computer skills used daily for tracking, scheduling, reporting, or analysis (pivot tables, formulas, structured trackers expected). Working knowledge of numbers and finance (budgets, revenues, costs, simple financial analysis, or commercial decision-making). Demonstrated ability to operate under urgency, including handling last-minute requests, changing priorities, and high-visibility tasks with accuracy. Experience working with senior stakeholders is an advantage but not essential if behavioural maturity is strong. Skills Strong prioritization and execution skills. Ability to stay calm and effective under pressure. Professional discretion and confidentiality. We’re here to provide excellent service but a little help from you can ensure a five-star candidate experience from start to finish. Before you click “apply”: Please read the job description carefully to ensure you can confidently demonstrate why this opportunity is right for you and take the time to put together a well-crafted and personalised CV to further boost your visibility. Our global Talent Acquisition team members are all assigned to specific businesses to ensure that we make the best matches between talent and opportunities. We not only consider the requisite compatibility of skills and behaviours, but also how candidates align with our Values of Respect, Integrity, Collaboration, and Excellence. As part of our candidate experience promise, we also want to make ourselves available to you throughout the application process. We make every effort to review and respond to every application.

review_candidates.title: Supply Chain Expert (SSA, L10)
review_candidates.description: DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 10 September 2026-23:59-GMT+02:00 Eastern European Standard Time (Cairo) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok. WHY JOIN WFP? WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: The World Food Programme (WFP) has extensive global experience in supporting governments to design, strengthen and scale sustainable National School Feeding Programmes (NSFPs). Under its School Feeding Strategy (2020–2030), WFP prioritizes national ownership by helping countries enhance systems, improve programme quality, and test innovative approaches tailored to their context. Egypt currently operates one of the world’s largest school feeding programmes, reaching over 13 million children. However, the model relies predominantly on fortified biscuits with limited nutritional diversity due to logistical, safety and infrastructure constraints. In line with national strategies, including Vision 2030, the Education Sector Plan and the National Food and Nutrition Strategy, the Government, through the Minister of Education, is exploring the possibility of shifting toward providing fresh, nutritious hot meals, reaffirming commitments made under the School Meals Coalition. To support this transition, the Minister of Education has formally requested WFP’s assistance in designing a scalable, cost efficient national hot meal model, covering operational guidance, infrastructure mapping, procurement and supply chain strengthening and the integration of lessons from global best practice. As a foundational step, WFP and the Ministry of Education and Technical Education (MoETE) will undertake a comprehensive mapping of school, community, and market capacities relevant to hot meal delivery, and to conduct a feasibility analysis to classify schools according to their readiness for transition during the 2026/2027 academic year. WFP seeks the services of a Supply Chain Expert to provide specialist advice, analytics and contributions to integrated supply chain operations to ensure the design of effective and integrated supply chain approach that will inform the transition from snack based school feeding to a national hot/fresh school meals programme. The expert should have broad experience across procurement, service delivery systems, operational design, contract management, costing, and logistics to support the development of a scalable and sustainable national hot school meals model. The incumbent will work through the WFP Egypt CO in close collaboration with MoETE at central, governorate, and district levels to ensure alignment with national rules and regulations. WHY JOIN WFP EGYPT? Contribute to one of the largest school feeding transformation initiatives globally. Support a high-impact programme expected to improve access to nutritious meals for millions of children. Work alongside government counterparts, technical experts and international stakeholders. Apply your expertise to influence relevant national supply chains and service delivery models. SCOPE Thematic Scope: The scope of this assignment falls within the WFP’s support to enhance Egypt’s national school feeding programme, focusing on assessing the readiness of the system to transition to safe and efficient hot/fresh meal provision. For that, a comprehensive examination of the infrastructure and operational conditions required for such a shift to understand existing capacities for meal production, storage, and delivery. Based on the feasibility assessment, a collection of context-appropriate delivery models will be developed, including guidance on costs, staffing, equipment, logistics, safety, and nutrition standards. To operate hot meals at scale, there is need to operationalize a procurement and supply chain system capable of ensuring food safety and quality, predictability, and cost-efficiency. Temporal Scope: The assignment is expected to commence in the coming months and continue through the rollout of the programme for the 2026/2027 school year, subject to project timelines and funding availability. Geographic Scope: Nationwide. TYPE OF CONTRACT: Special Service Agreement (SSA, L10) DUTY STATION (City, Country): Cairo, Egypt DURATION: 6 months ACCOUNTABILITIES: Provide technical guidance on supply‑chain‑related data collection for the national mapping, covering market access, supplier proximity, cold chain and storage availability, transport corridors, and the presence of caterers, community kitchens, NGOs, and private operators, and contribute to the infrastructure gap analysis by defining minimum logistics and supply chain requirements per school cluster. Analyze local market functionality in priority governorates, including availability, seasonality, price stability, supplier capacity, and associated supply chain risks (food safety, inflation, transport reliability), and propose preliminary mitigation measures. Provide technical inputs into the design of on‑site, central kitchen, and hybrid delivery models, including end‑to‑end supply chain flows, indicative logistics, staffing, storage needs, cost drivers, and operational constraints by geography and school cluster. Lead development of procurement and supply chain strategy options aligned with national regulations, covering local sourcing, centralized and decentralized procurement modalities, contracting of caterers and service providers, framework agreements, quality assurance and food safety controls, and initial options for digital traceability and monitoring systems. Provide detailed supply chain inputs to costing and financial models, including logistics unit costs, scenario and sensitivity analysis (fuel, distance, inflation), and implications of local sourcing levels across delivery models. Draft and/or review supply chain sections of the National Operational Manual, including SOPs for procurement, storage, transport, inventory management, roles and responsibilities, performance indicators, and identification of capacity‑strengthening needs for government and implementation partners. Assess technical capacity and develop a related training programme for national stakeholders with a Training of Trainers focus. Support supply chain readiness for phased start‑up by validating assumptions for selected governorates, advising on tendering and contracting technical inputs, identifying early operational bottlenecks and mitigation actions, and contributing to a short lessons‑learned and adjustment note to inform scale‑up. Provide ad-hoc support to national counterparts during pilot stage. Any other related duties, as required, within the scope of the assignment. Deliverables Supply Chain Mapping and Feasibility Input Report A concise report consolidating supply‑chain inputs to the national mapping and feasibility work, including analysis of market functionality, supplier and logistics capacity, storage and cold‑chain availability, and key supply‑chain risks affecting hot meal delivery. Hot School Meals Supply Chain & Procurement Strategy A streamlined strategy outlining end‑to‑end supply chain designs for on‑site, central kitchen, and hybrid models, with recommended procurement and contracting modalities, local sourcing options, and key food safety and quality assurance considerations. Supply Chain Costing and Operational Guidance Package A practical package providing supply‑chain cost assumptions and sensitivity inputs for financial modelling, alongside draft supply‑chain sections for the National Operational Manual covering procurement, storage, transport, inventory management, and performance monitoring. Capacity Assessment and TOT Capacity Assessment of supply chain relevant stakeholders and TOT delivered Start‑up Readiness and Scale‑up Adjustment Note A short, action‑oriented note assessing supply‑chain readiness for phased implementation, highlighting early operational bottlenecks, mitigation measures, and recommended adjustments to inform initial roll‑out and scale‑up. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations, Economics, Engineering, or a related field. A first-level degree with additional relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree. Experience: At least 8–10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in supply chain, logistics, procurement, operations design, or related fields, including a minimum of 5 years providing senior technical or advisory support. Proven experience designing, implementing, or strengthening end-to-end supply chain and service delivery systems, ideally covering a combination of procurement, catering or food service operations, facility or service design, logistics, contract management, costing, and operational planning. Experience in institutional catering, hospitality, airline catering, large-scale food service operations, school feeding, healthcare, or comparable sectors is highly desirable. Demonstrated experience in costing, financial modelling, and analysis of operational and supply chain solutions, including assessment of cost drivers, efficiency opportunities, and delivery models. Experience managing or advising on procurement strategies, supplier engagement, contracting modalities, and performance management of service providers. Strong understanding of food safety and quality standards and their application across food procurement, production, storage, transport, and service delivery systems is highly desirable. Experience supporting large-scale public sector, food systems, nutrition, school feeding, or social protection programmes is highly desirable. Demonstrated experience working with government counterparts and contributing to policy, strategy, or operational guidance at national or sub-national level. Knowledge & Skills Strong knowledge of procurement and contracting modalities, supply chain design, food safety and quality assurance systems, storage, transport, logistics, and service delivery operations. Sound understanding of large-scale food service, catering, or institutional meal delivery systems, including operational, infrastructure, and supplier management considerations. Proven ability to assess and develop cost-effective supply chain and service delivery models, including costing assumptions, operational requirements, and performance monitoring frameworks. Strong analytical, report-writing, and drafting skills, with the ability to produce clear, practical technical guidance and recommendations for government and senior decision makers. Demonstrated stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills, with the ability to work effectively with government counterparts, service providers, and technical experts. Ability to work independently and deliver high-quality outputs under tight timelines. Languages: Fluency in written and spoken English and Arabic required.
